source_review.notes: Checked current ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 lifecycle scope and concurrency statement, ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017 software lifecycle material, and SWEBOK v4.0a process/maintenance coverage. Foundational flow, systems, and improvement sources support durable claims.

evidence: Reviewed activity-contract tuple, dependency and feedback edges, loop tuple, latency decomposition, exposure approximation, WIP age, flow time, and throughput definitions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes approximate exposure from actual harm and distinguishes activity dependencies from feedback revisions.

evidence: Executed feedback-loop-audit and independently recomputed exposures 0.08, 2.00, and 56.00 at four changes/day.
Verified complete count 2 and attention count 1 from loop fields.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All printed delay and exposure values match exact deterministic arithmetic; no real risk magnitude is inferred.

evidence: Re-derived total latency as observation, transport, interpretation, decision, and action delay.
Re-derived lifecycle dependency/feedback network and nested-loop portfolio.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The exposure relationship is explicitly an approximation under constant-rate assumptions, not a universal theorem.

evidence: Reviewed zero/long delay, invalid/flaky signal, missing owner/action/re-observation, large batch, saturated queue, stale data, emergency change, incident recurrence, hidden consumer, and retirement-monitoring cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Fast signals never bypass validity or authority; safety and retirement boundaries require explicit evidence and escalation.

evidence: Traced activity contracts, lifecycle concurrency, verification/validation distinction, downstream-to-upstream learning, complete loops, WIP visibility, handoff return paths, and traceability.
invariant_checking.notes: Every activity/loop example preserves its evidence scope; process tailoring cannot silently remove an obligation.

evidence: Reviewed latency/exposure derivation and Boolean loop-completeness evaluation line by line.
Reviewed feedback compatibility and lifecycle completeness arguments.
proof_review.notes: The chapter makes no formal process-optimality or actual-harm proof; calculations are limited to the stated teaching model.

evidence: Audited uses of proves, evidence, model, invariant, exposure, risk, verification, and validation.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Examples, approximations, and standard-derived claims are labeled at their real evidence strength; no proof sketch is presented as a theorem.

evidence: Reviewed executable-output scope, standards currency, flow statements, and medical/railway limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The snippet is deterministic model evidence only. No productivity, safety effectiveness, certification, or external review claim is made.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed lifecycle activities versus models, concurrent/recursive application, feedback components, loop portfolios, verification/validation, delay, WIP, maintenance, incidents, security/safety, and retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed activity contracts, evidence gates, queue diagnosis, canary/data guardrails, incident learning, process experiments, handoff acceptance, emergency authority, and retirement closure. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from lifecycle obligations through complete loops and delay to operational learning/retirement; ten examples and five answered exercises provide distinct retrieval-to-safety transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
